name: Sleep
caption: Sleep

configuration.description: How long to wait, as a positive whole number in the chosen unit. Stored as text by the editor (e.g. "30"); a JSON number is also read. May be a SmartField token such as "{{RetryDelay_Seconds}}", resolved at runtime.
Time unit: 0 = Milliseconds, 1 = Seconds, 2 = Minutes, 3 = Hours. A missing, null or unknown value falls back to 1 (Seconds). The editor always writes it.

rules.check: configuration.duration must be present and non-empty
rules.message: Sleep step '%1' has no duration configured.

rules.check: configuration.duration must be a positive integer (> 0) or contain a SmartField token ('{{' followed later by '}}')
rules.message: Sleep step '%1' duration '%2' is not a positive integer or SmartField token.

rules.check: configuration.duration must be non-empty (required field in the configuration dialog). The editor does not check that it is a number.
rules.message: Please fill in the highlighted fields.

rules.check: The resolved duration must parse as an integer > 0
rules.message: Sleep duration '%1' is not a positive integer.

rules.check: A deferring sleep (unit other than Milliseconds, or >= 10000 ms) is not allowed when the flow runs synchronously (for example the webhook synchronous phase, a SubFlow body, interactive document or page triggers, PDF hooks)
rules.message: Step %1 (%2) requested a deferred resume, but the flow is running synchronously. Use Sleep or other time-based deferral steps only outside of synchronous frames (Webhook sync phase or SubFlow body).

notes: Strategy: unit Milliseconds with a duration below 10000 blocks the worker in-process (System sleep). Any other unit, or 10000 ms and more, defers: the run is parked with status Sleeping, and a single-run job queue entry resumes it at now + duration. On resume, the step completes immediately and the flow continues.
Deferral means a background job-queue resume. It cannot happen inside a synchronous frame. In those, only short millisecond sleeps (< 10 s) work.
The publish warnings use the step id (not the description) as %1.
Leading zeros are accepted by the integer parse. Decimal values (e.g. '1.5') are not accepted.
unit must be a JSON integer. A number outside 0-3 silently becomes Seconds, but a non-numeric value such as "Minutes" cannot be converted and fails the step (and the editor) with a platform error.
